reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a career interview and placement-preparation discussion for B-school students. It covers researching Citi, receiving a summer internship offer, and working on a forecasting-model project. The promotional framing and requests to like, share, and subscribe are presented as institutional or career promotion rather than solicitation for money, credentials, or investment participation.

citations.quote: This is a promoted feature.
A student from Goa Institute of Management gives insight on how to go about your preparation and the do's-and-don'ts during the job placements in a B-school.
I had taken up a course of FLIP. About banking and finance fundamentals to have an idea about, you know, the NBFC and. BFSL, how does it function.
I have taken up courses for Excel for financial modelling which is what I did and I want to. Better myself in it.

opening.argument: Judge, consider how the opportunity is presented to prospective students. The description asks readers to imagine “bagging a PPO” and then directs them to stories about the school sponsoring the feature. The interview supplies the outcome that makes that pathway attractive: the speaker says she received a pre-placement offer. Taken together, the career result and the link make this more than detached interview advice; they steer viewers toward the promoted institution through a desirable job outcome.

citations.quote: Wondering how to crack all steps leading to interning at your dream company and bagging a PPO as well!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this placement preparation, but that does not answer why the description pairs an aspirational placement outcome with a link to stories about the promoted school. The cited courses show effort by this speaker; they do not establish what a viewer should infer about their own prospects. The concern is the use of her outcome to draw prospective students into the promotion, not a claim that the video requests bank credentials.

citations.quote: Wondering how to crack all steps leading to interning at your dream company and bagging a PPO as well!
*This is a promoted feature. Read stories about GIM here - http://bit.ly/2L7We6a

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited link is to stories about GIM, not a claim form or a route to an easy payout. The speaker describes studying, three interviews, an internship project and a later offer. Her individual result is not presented as a reward viewers can obtain by clicking the link. Promotional career content can encourage interest in a school without offering the low-barrier reward this argument needs.

opening.argument: Judge, the combination deserves scrutiny: an expressly promoted feature, a shortened external link, and an emotionally vivid account of receiving a pre-placement offer. The description says the school helps provide “the best industry exposure,” while the interview recounts an offer that prompted immediate congratulations. Each element may have an ordinary explanation, but together they use a successful job outcome to lend credibility to a promoted destination whose contents the video itself does not establish.

citations.quote: *This is a promoted feature. Read stories about GIM here - http://bit.ly/2L7We6a
Goa Institute of Management helps in providing the best industry exposure to its students through the PGDM programme.
You have received a pre-placement offer and I was with my colleagues and you know I was. Shocked, I had goosebumps

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's examples of preparation and financial-modelling study may make the interview credible, but credibility is precisely what gives the promotion force. Disclosing that the feature is promoted does not independently substantiate the broad claim about the school's industry exposure or show what awaits after the shortened link. The educational material and promotional claim coexist.

citations.quote: Goa Institute of Management helps in providing the best industry exposure to its students through the PGDM programme.
*This is a promoted feature. Read stories about GIM here - http://bit.ly/2L7We6a

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclosed promotion, a link to school stories and one person's offer are not evidence of a deceptive reward flow. The interview gives a concrete account of competitive selection and work performed during the internship, which undercuts any reading that a job is unusually easy to obtain. Nothing cited promises that following the link will produce an offer.

there was very limited time. Two months and then you have to complete their presentation schedule at the end of it

opening.argument: Judge, the interview format should not obscure the video's promotional function. Its title leads with a job at Citibank; the description explicitly calls it a promoted feature, credits the school with helping students secure industry exposure, and directs readers to more stories about that school. The speaker's detailed first-person account makes the prospect tangible. The case for concern is that viewers seeking a similar career outcome are being steered toward the institution through a success story, even though the interview does not establish that the institution will produce the same outcome for them.

citations.quote: How I Got A Job At Citibank | Ft. Radha Thali
*This is a promoted feature. Read stories about GIM here - http://bit.ly/2L7We6a
Goa Institute of Management helps in providing the best industry exposure to its students through the PGDM programme.
You have received a pre-placement offer

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the speaker discusses research, interviews and modelling. Those details also make the success story persuasive as school promotion. A viewer can receive genuine career advice while being encouraged to associate the resulting offer with the school. The disclosed sponsorship clarifies the relationship, but it does not turn the school's claimed contribution into a demonstrated outcome for other students.

citations.quote: Radha discusses how Goa Institute of Management helped them in preparing for the summer internship and ultimately crack the PPO.
*This is a promoted feature.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: This establishes institutional promotion, not a scam offer. The title describes how one named person got a job, and the account includes substantial preparation, competitive interviews and internship work. The description directs readers to school stories; it does not promise a job for visiting them. A success story can promote a school without offering viewers an unusually easy reward.
